clue.text: One's embracing and not about to display restraint

definitions.note: the answer is plural, the shackles that make up a restraint

indicators.note: embracing means the outer piece wraps its arms round the inner one

parts.note: one gives I and the 's is the S that follows it

indicators.note: about tells us to turn the word for 'and not' back to front

parts.note: 'and not' is nor, as in 'neither this nor that'

explanation.surface: Someone who doesn't fuss about anything showing self-control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' gives both the I and the S that wrap round; 'restraint' stands for a set of shackles.
explanation.definitionFit: Irons are fetters or shackles, a physical form of restraint on a prisoner.

clue.text: Arouse love to block evil hostile action

parts.note: to incur anger is to arouse it

indicators.note: to block means love plugs a gap inside the evil

parts.note: sin is evil
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: Stirring up love to stop wickedness.
explanation.definitionFit: An incursion is a raid or invasion into enemy territory.

clue.text: Dead-headed rose, used bladed implement

indicators.note: dead-headed, like a spent flower, means the first letter is taken off

parts.note: rose as a verb, went up, soared

explanation.surface: A gardener deadheading roses with a cutting tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rose' looks like the flower but is the past tense of rise.
explanation.definitionFit: A rower pulls a bladed oar through the water, so rowing is using a bladed implement.

clue.text: Sandwich with fruit, awesome

parts.note: a sub is a submarine sandwich
a lime is a citrus fruit

explanation.surface: A sandwich with fruit, which is amazing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sublime is so grand or exalted it inspires awe.

clue.text: Right routes to block South American's acerbity

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south

indicators.note: to block means the pieces sit inside and plug the other pair of letters

parts.note: American gives US; the 's is a link meaning is
lines are routes, as in railway or bus lines

explanation.surface: A traveller complaining that the roads impede a South American, which makes for sourness.
explanation.definitionFit: Acerbity is sharpness of temper, the same bad-tempered rudeness as grumpiness.

clue.text: Damage agricultural tool scrubbing yard for head of abbey

indicators.note: scrubbing means a letter is wiped out of the tool
for means another letter takes its place

parts.note: a scythe is a long-bladed farm tool for mowing

indicators.note: head of picks the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A farm tool wrecking a yard before an abbot takes charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To scathe is an old verb meaning to harm or injure, as in unscathed.

clue.text: Basic uniform, stupid to get torn outside

definitions.note: basic here is a noun, one of the basics

indicators.note: outside means the torn word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: rent is the past participle of rend, to tear
U is uniform in the NATO alphabet
dim means stupid

explanation.surface: A plain uniform, foolishly ripped on the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Basic' reads as an adjective with 'uniform' but stands as a noun, one of the basics.
explanation.definitionFit: A rudiment is a first principle, one of the elementary basics of a subject.

clue.text: Come into popular hospital weary, on reflection

parts.note: in means popular, fashionable

indicators.note: on reflection means the tiring word is mirrored, read backwards

parts.note: to weary is to tire

explanation.surface: Coming into a busy hospital and feeling worn out, thinking it over.
explanation.definitionFit: To come into money is to receive it from someone's estate, by succession.

clue.text: Gold that is found in surgical department makes one exuberant

indicators.note: found in means the pieces sit inside the department

parts.note: ENT is ear, nose and throat, a hospital department
the bull is the gold centre of an archery target
ie is id est, that is

explanation.surface: Finding gold in an operating unit makes someone overjoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gold' is not bullion but the bull, the gold centre of a target.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebullient means bubbling over with enthusiasm, full of high spirits.

clue.text: Uncool fellow's weird when turning up

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means the letters read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: odd means weird
as means when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A dull man is strange whenever he arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: A saddo is British slang for a pathetic, socially inept person, a loser.

clue.text: A way swine butts into recording material

indicators.note: butts into means the group of pieces pushes its way inside the outer pair

parts.note: a CD is a recording on compact disc
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way
a boar is a male swine

explanation.surface: A pig barging into a recording studio's stock of supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiff pasteboard is a material used for packaging and boxes.

clue.text: Harry Houdini, bereft of any ego, struggling

definitions.note: to harry is a verb, to pester or chase relentlessly

indicators.note: struggling suggests the letters writhing about, as the escapologist did, into a new order
bereft of means the letters named are removed

parts.note: the ego is I, and 'any' means every I goes, both of them

explanation.surface: The escapologist Harry Houdini, stripped of his vanity, fighting to get free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like Houdini's first name but is the verb. Removing both I's leaves HOUDN, which 'struggling' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry someone is to pursue and pester them relentlessly, as a dog chases quarry.

clue.text: Like some wine poured after halfway through meal?

indicators.note: after halfway through points to the letters that come once the midpoint of the word is passed, its back half

parts.note: a dish is a course or meal served at table

explanation.surface: A question about wine served once a dinner is half over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after halfway through' takes the second half of 'poured', RED.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosé and some light wines have a tinge of red colour, a reddish hue.

clue.text: Fungus left over that's used in some brandies

definitions.note: a description standing for the fruit itself, a cherry

parts.note: a morel is an edible fungus
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Mushroom remnants turning up in brandy.
explanation.walkthrough: An over in cricket is a set of six balls.
explanation.definitionFit: This sour dark cherry is steeped in brandy to make cherry brandy.

clue.text: In recess, house contains silver idols

indicators.note: contains means the reversed house holds the silver inside it
in recess read as receding, going back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a semi is a semi-detached house
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A house tucked away in an alcove holding silver statues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In recess' looks like a place but signals that SEMI recedes to IMES.
explanation.definitionFit: Idols are statues or likenesses worshipped as gods, carved figures.

clue.text: Tackled by a biter bizarrely, inform referee

definitions.note: referee as a verb, to umpire

indicators.note: tackled by means the informer is grabbed and held inside
bizarrely means the letters of 'a biter' are strangely rearranged

parts.note: to rat is to inform on someone

explanation.surface: A footballer bitten in a strange tackle telling the match official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bizarrely' makes ARBITE from A BITER, and RAT goes in before the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: To arbitrate is to judge a dispute as an impartial umpire.

clue.text: King died, pierced by apparently large invader in the garden

indicators.note: pierced by means the second piece is driven inside the first pair

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
large put as a negative, not wee, wee being Scottish for small

explanation.surface: A king dies, stabbed by a seemingly huge intruder in the grounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Japanese knotweed is a notoriously invasive plant that takes over gardens.

clue.text: Doctor hosting private therapy primarily to stop economic decline

indicators.note: hosting means the doctor holds the other letters inside

parts.note: own means private, one's own

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of the next word

parts.note: to end is to stop

explanation.surface: A doctor offering private treatment, mainly to halt a slump.
explanation.definitionFit: A downward trend in markets or the economy is a decline.

clue.text: Made respectful gesture, better to welcome in first to turn up

indicators.note: to welcome in means the healed word takes the other letters inside

parts.note: better as a past participle, made well again

indicators.note: to turn up in a down clue means the letters are reversed

parts.note: 1st is first, read with the 1 as I

explanation.surface: A better person greeting the first guest to arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' means healed, CURED. 'to turn up' turns IST (1st) into TSI.
explanation.definitionFit: A curtsy is a bob made by bending the knees, a deferential gesture.

clue.text: Vague posh character twice interrupting nobles, excitedly

indicators.note: excitedly means the letters of nobles are stirred up into a new order
twice means the posh letter is used two times

parts.note: U stands for upper-class, a posh character

explanation.surface: Excited aristocrats being butted into by some toff, and nothing clear emerges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interrupting' puts the two U's into different places in NEBLOS, the anagram of NOBLES from 'excitedly', so the parse pools all eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nebulous is hazy and ill-defined, like a cloud: indistinct.

clue.text: Dance graduate in foreign car

indicators.note: in means the graduate sits inside the car

parts.note: a Lada is a Russian make of car
an MBA is a Master of Business Administration graduate

explanation.surface: A dancing graduate inside a foreign vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively Brazilian partner dance, a craze of the late 1980s.

clue.text: Vessel in reverse to drag fawn

indicators.note: in reverse means the cooking vessel is written backwards

parts.note: a wok is a cooking vessel
to tow is to drag along

explanation.surface: A boat backing up to pull a young deer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fawn' is the verb, to grovel, not the young deer.
explanation.definitionFit: To kowtow is to grovel obsequiously, just as to fawn is to flatter servilely.

clue.text: Take ordinary engineering item

definitions.note: a take is a view, as in 'what's your take on it?'

parts.note: a pinion is a small cogwheel

explanation.surface: Picking up an everyday mechanical part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take' looks like a verb but is a noun: someone's view.
explanation.definitionFit: Your take on something is your view or belief about it.

clue.text: Avoid the computing scene?

parts.note: the prefix e- marks electronic or computing things, as in email
-scape means a scene, as in landscape

explanation.surface: Steer clear of the tech world?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the split E-SCAPE is not a real word for a computing scene.
explanation.definitionFit: To evade something is to elude or get away from it.

clue.text: Initially, angler takes bait and tackle

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of each of the next two words

parts.note: to bait is to lure or tempt

explanation.surface: An angler starts by taking bait and fishing gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tackle' looks like fishing gear but is the verb, to have a go.
explanation.definitionFit: To tackle a job is to have a go at it, to try it.

clue.text: Mythological figure a sailor upset

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: an old salt is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor knocked over by a figure from legend.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titan in Greek myth condemned to hold up the heavens.

clue.text: Cutting class, about to go quickly and quietly

indicators.note: about means the class wraps round the other letters

parts.note: a set is a class or group, as in school sets
to nip is to go quickly, as in nip to the shops
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Skipping a lesson, someone about to slip off fast and silently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting' looks like skipping class but is a noun: a clipping.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutting from a newspaper is a small clipped extract, a scrap of text.

clue.text: Stunt, parking where taxis park

parts.note: P is the symbol for parking
a taxi rank is where cabs wait

explanation.surface: A stunt involving parking at a cab stand.
explanation.definitionFit: A stunt can be a practical joke or trick, a jape.

clue.text: Asian city wall has angry guards

indicators.note: guards means the words hold the answer inside them, as guards surround a prisoner

explanation.surface: An Asian city whose wall shelters furious guards.
explanation.definitionFit: This city is the capital of Tibet, in Asia.

clue.text: Dull auntie oddly entertained by prisoner

indicators.note: entertained by means the odd letters are taken in as guests by the prisoner

parts.note: an inmate is a prisoner

indicators.note: oddly picks the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A boring aunt, strangely, being hosted by a convict.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifeless and lacking spirit, an inert thing is dull.

clue.text: Shoot from cultivated leeks cut by father and daughter

definitions.note: shoot as an imperative, clear off

indicators.note: cut by means the scrambled leeks are split by the letters going inside
cultivated means the leeks are worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: dad is father

explanation.surface: A sprout from a vegetable patch of leeks, sliced up by dad and his girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoot' looks like a sprout from the leeks but means scram. 'cultivated' turns LEEKS into SKELE, which DADD splits.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoot! is an exclamation telling someone to go away fast, to scram.

clue.text: Cheesed off after run's left uncovered

indicators.note: left means the run has departed from the word

parts.note: narked is British slang for annoyed, cheesed off
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone annoyed after a jog to find they have been left exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: Narked and cheesed off are both British slang for irritated.
explanation.definitionFit: Naked means bare, without clothes or any covering.
